In the 1860s, aided by soldiers playing the game in camp during the [Civil War](/wiki/American_Civil_War "American Civil War"), "New York"-style baseball expanded into a national game and spawned baseball's first governing body, the [National Association of Base Ball Players](/wiki/National_Association_of_Base_Ball_Players "National Association of Base Ball Players") (NABBP). The NABBP existed as an amateur league for 12 years. By 1867, more than 400 clubs were members. Most of the strongest clubs remained those based in the northeastern United States. For [professional baseball](/wiki/Professional_baseball "Professional baseball")'s founding year, MLB uses the year 1869—when the first professional team, the [Cincinnati Red Stockings](/wiki/Cincinnati_Red_Stockings "Cincinnati Red Stockings"), was established.[[27]](#cite_note-27)

A schism developed between professional and amateur ballplayers after the founding of the Cincinnati club. The NABBP split into an amateur organization and a professional organization. The [National Association of Professional Base Ball Players](/wiki/National_Association_of_Professional_Base_Ball_Players "National Association of Professional Base Ball Players"), often known as the National Association (NA), was formed in 1871.[[28]](#cite_note-base_ball-28) Its amateur counterpart disappeared after only a few years.[[29]](#cite_note-Rader-29) The modern [Chicago Cubs](/wiki/Chicago_Cubs "Chicago Cubs") and [Atlanta Braves](/wiki/Atlanta_Braves "Atlanta Braves") franchises trace their histories back to the National Association of Professional Base Ball Players in the 1870s.[[30]](#cite_note-Spatz-30)

In 1876, the National League of Professional Base Ball Clubs (later known as the [National League](/wiki/National_League_(baseball) "National League (baseball)") or NL) was established after the NA proved ineffective. The league placed its emphasis on clubs rather than on players. Clubs could now enforce player contracts, preventing players from jumping to higher-paying clubs. fanoutqa_032222.x:
Anton Zeilinger :: Research :: Neutron interferometry :: chunk_0007
Anton Zeilinger's earliest work is perhaps his least known. His work on neutron interferometry has provided a foundation for his later research.[[15]](#cite_note-Del_Santo_2022-15)

As a member of the group of his thesis supervisor, [Helmut Rauch](/wiki/Helmut_Rauch "Helmut Rauch"), at the [Technical University of Vienna](/wiki/Vienna_University_of_Technology "Vienna University of Technology"), Zeilinger participated in a number of neutron interferometry experiments at the [Institut Laue–Langevin](/wiki/Institut_Laue%E2%80%93Langevin "Institut Laue–Langevin") (ILL) in Grenoble. His very first such experiment confirmed a fundamental prediction of quantum mechanics, the sign change of a spinor phase upon rotation.[[51]](#cite_note-51) This was followed by the first experimental realization of coherent spin superposition of [matter waves](/wiki/Matter_waves "Matter waves"). He continued his work in [neutron interferometry](/wiki/Neutron_interferometry "Neutron interferometry") at [MIT](/wiki/MIT "MIT") with [C.G. Shull](/wiki/Clifford_Shull "Clifford Shull") ([Nobel Laureate](/wiki/Nobel_Laureate "Nobel Laureate")), focusing specifically on dynamical diffraction effects of [neutrons](/wiki/Neutrons "Neutrons") in perfect crystals which are due to multi-wave coherent superposition. After his return to Europe, he built up an interferometer for very cold neutrons which preceded later similar experiments with atoms. The fundamental experiments there included a most precise test of the linearity of quantum mechanics. Zeilinger built a [double-slit diffraction experiment](/wiki/Double-slit_experiment "Double-slit experiment")[[52]](#cite_note-52) on the S18 instrument at the [Institut Laue-Langevin](/wiki/Institut_Laue%E2%80%93Langevin "Institut Laue–Langevin") which, later on, gained in accuracy and could act with only one neutron at a time in the apparatus.[[53]](#cite_note-53)

The Dodgers were the first Major League Baseball team to ever play in Los Angeles. On April 18, 1958, the Dodgers played their first Los Angeles game, defeating the former New York and now new [San Francisco Giants](/wiki/1958_San_Francisco_Giants_season "1958 San Francisco Giants season"), 6–5, before 78,672 fans at the [Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum](/wiki/Los_Angeles_Memorial_Coliseum "Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum"). The [1959 World Series](/wiki/1959_World_Series "1959 World Series") was played partially at the [Los Angeles Coliseum](/wiki/Los_Angeles_Coliseum "Los Angeles Coliseum") while Dodger Stadium was being built.

Construction on [Dodger Stadium](/wiki/Dodger_Stadium "Dodger Stadium") was completed in time for Opening Day 1962. With its clean, simple lines and its picturesque setting amid hills and palm trees, the ballpark quickly became an icon of the Dodgers and their new California lifestyle. O'Malley was determined that there would not be a bad seat in the house, achieving this by [cantilevered](/wiki/Cantilever "Cantilever") grandstands that have since been widely imitated. More importantly for the team, the stadium's spacious dimensions, along with other factors, gave defense an advantage over offense and the Dodgers moved to take advantage of this by assembling a team that would excel with its [pitching](/wiki/Pitch_(baseball) "Pitch (baseball)").

The university was founded in Beijing by the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) in September 1958.[[2]](#cite_note-:3-2) The director of CAS, [Guo Moruo](/wiki/Guo_Moruo "Guo Moruo") was appointed the first president of USTC. USTC's founding mission was to develop a high-level science and technology workforce, as deemed critical for the development of China's economy, defense, and science and technology education. The establishment was hailed as "A Major Event in the History of Chinese Education and Science." CAS has supported USTC by combining most of its institutes with the departments of the university. In 1959, USTC was listed in the top 16 [national key universities](/wiki/National_Key_Universities "National Key Universities"), becoming the youngest national key university.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

At the beginning of 1970, the university moved to Hefei during the Cultural Revolution.[[3]](#cite_note-:4-3)

In 2012, USTC and the [National University of Defense Technology](/wiki/National_University_of_Defense_Technology "National University of Defense Technology") signed a strategic agreement to cooperate on [quantum computing](/wiki/Quantum_computing "Quantum computing") research at a ceremony attended by [Pan Jianwei](/wiki/Pan_Jianwei "Pan Jianwei") and [Yang Xuejun](/wiki/Yang_Xuejun "Yang Xuejun").[[6]](#cite_note-6)

**Bahrain**,[[a]](#cite_note-17) officially the **Kingdom of Bahrain**,[[b]](#cite_note-18) is an [island country](/wiki/Island_country "Island country") in [West Asia](/wiki/West_Asia "West Asia"). Situated near the western shore of the [Persian Gulf](/wiki/Persian_Gulf "Persian Gulf") and latitudinally about two-thirds the shore's length from the north, the country comprises a small [archipelago](/wiki/Archipelago "Archipelago") of 33 natural islands and an additional 50 [artificial islands](/wiki/Artificial_island "Artificial island"), centered on [Bahrain Island](/wiki/Bahrain_Island "Bahrain Island"), which makes up around 80 percent of the country's landmass. [Insects](/wiki/Insect "Insect"), a [class](/wiki/Class_(biology) "Class (biology)") of [Arthropoda](/wiki/Arthropod "Arthropod"), are easily the most numerous class of organisms, with over one million identified species, and probably many undescribed species. The heaviest insect is almost certainly a species of [beetle](/wiki/Coleoptera "Coleoptera"), which incidentally is the most species-rich order of organisms. Although heavyweight [giant wētās](/wiki/Giant_w%C4%93t%C4%81 "Giant wētā") (*[Deinacrida heteracantha](/wiki/Deinacrida_heteracantha "Deinacrida heteracantha")*) are known, the [elephant beetles](/wiki/Elephant_beetle "Elephant beetle") of Central and South America, (*[Megasoma elephas](/wiki/Megasoma_elephas "Megasoma elephas")*) and (*[M. actaeon](/wiki/Megasoma_actaeon "Megasoma actaeon")*), the [Titan beetle](/wiki/Titan_beetle "Titan beetle") (*Titanus giganteus*) of the neotropical rainforest or the [Goliath beetles](/wiki/Goliathus "Goliathus"), (*[Goliathus goliatus](/wiki/Goliathus_goliatus "Goliathus goliatus")*) and (*[G. regius](/wiki/Goliathus_regius "Goliathus regius")*), of Africa's rainforest are thought to reach a higher weight.[[296]](#cite_note-weta-296) The most frequently crowned are the Goliath beetles, the top known size of which is at least 100 g (3.5 oz) and 11.5 cm (4.5 in).[[1]](#cite_note-Wood-1) The elephant beetles and titan beetle can reach greater lengths than the Goliath, at up to 13.1 and 15.2 cm (5.2 and 6.0 in), respectively, but this is in part thanks to their rather large horns. The Goliath beetle's wingspan can range up to 25 cm (9.8 in).[[1]](#cite_note-Wood-1)

Some moths and butterflies have much larger areas than the heaviest beetles, but weigh a fraction as much.
